title: The Salt Road Cartographers
author: Liv Hartikainen
authorBio: Liv Hartikainen writes adventure fantasy about maps, weather and stubborn people. She keeps a wall of unfinished atlases and sells none of them.
tagline: Someone is redrawing the land, and only Reet can prove it.
description: Every dawn, nineteen-year-old Reet Sallik rides out to redraw a map of a land that rearranges itself in the dark. When she notices the land obeying the Guild's locked atlas, she crosses the Seam with a disgraced mentor, a caravan guard and an ink-maker's son.
contentNotes: Peril, a past disaster with loss of life, and a villain with a real moral argument.

title: Murder at the Marigold Bindery
author: Hester Pryce-Lowell
authorBio: Hester Pryce-Lowell grew up on the Cornish coast and spent thirty years repairing books in a small workshop. She lives near Truro with a stubborn cat.
tagline: A bookbinder reads a murder in thread, paste and paper.
description: When the village collector is found dead in her press room beside a half-sewn manuscript, widowed bookbinder Dot Pellow sees what the police cannot: the book has been rebound, twice. With a book fair in full swing, a regatta looming and eight suspects, she must read the clues before the killer reads her.

title: The Ninth Floor
author: Dominic Vasko
authorBio: Dominic Vasko writes crime fiction set among docks, hotels and rain. He has worked nights in more buildings than he admits to, and still counts the floors.
tagline: Eight buttons in the elevator. A dead man on the ninth.
description: November 1952. Night clerk Teddy Wozniak swears he found a dead guest on the Harbor Hotel's ninth floor. The building has eight. Ruth Szymanski, a former police dispatcher with the rent overdue, takes the case, and the lies begin at the front desk.
contentNotes: Murder, a death in custody, fear of deportation, and period prejudice.

title: Zero-Day Lullaby
author: Kasper Lindahl
authorBio: Kasper Lindahl writes fiction about people who work nights in quiet buildings. He lives in Tallinn and Turku, and learned to read spectrograms before he learned to cook.
tagline: A hospital hums a lullaby at three a.m. Someone is listening.
description: At three in the morning a neonatal ward's smart speakers hum the same lullaby, and Tallinn incident responder Ilse Kantor, deaf in one ear, learns what the tune is carrying. With nine days to a Helsinki summit, her old mentor keeps secrets, and everyone hunting the code has reason to hunt her.
contentNotes: Murder (off the page), surveillance and paranoia, a sick infant ward; no children are harmed on the page.

title: Unit 4B Does Not Exist
author: Tobias Nwosu
authorBio: Tobias Nwosu writes about offices, landlords and the small print of ordinary life. He grew up above a dry cleaner's and now lives in a building whose numbering he has stopped trusting.
tagline: The rent has always been paid. The unit has never existed.
description: Dev Mahajan types rent rolls for a property company, and the new software refuses to save one row: Apartment 4B, paying on time, with no door, no floor plan and no permit. Told to delete it, Dev walks the fourth floor instead, counting his steps, while the building starts to count him.
contentNotes: Grief for a parent, loneliness and isolation, a disappearance, the death of an elderly man from illness, and a bittersweet ending.

title: The Marquess's Misprint
author: Georgiana Fenwick
authorBio: Georgiana Fenwick writes comedies of manners from a Kentish cottage with a leaking roof and a cat named after a type size. This is her fourth novel.
tagline: One misprint, one marquess, and the printer's daughter who set it.
description: London, 1816: a cold, wet Season and one wrong line in the Gazette. Winifred Pargeter, a printer's daughter, has set the type that engages her to the Marquess of Stanmere, who finds the mistake rather convenient. Now the two must keep a lie alive in print, while a rival printer sharpens his pencil.
contentNotes: Debt and the threat of prison; bereavement; a parent who left.
